passages.text: Below the Pantry of Respawning Cheese, in a corner no one has swept, there is a door. It is a very small door. It hums.
A small voice from inside says: "Password?"

choices.text: Say nothing. Stare at the door.

passages.text: "Wrong," says the voice, "but admirably polite." The door swings open.
"Correct," says the voice. "It was always cheese." The door swings open.
The voice waits. You wait. Eleven years pass. Somewhere a goblin makes a tally mark.
The handle is locked. A tiny keyhole stares back at you, unimpressed.

choices.text: Try the ring of suspicious keys.

passages.text: One of the keys fits. None of them should. The door clicks open.
Beyond is a tiny library holding exactly one book, titled "The Door Below the Cheese". There is also a small chest, and a sign that says THIS ROOM IS NOT CANON.

choices.text: Read the book (it is this book).

passages.text: Inside the chest: a pile of gold, and a note in careful handwriting. "Well done. Now go touch grass."
You return upstairs. Behind you, the door goes on humming, a little disappointed.
The barkeep doesn't look up from the mug. "Ale's two gold. Bread's four. Rats are free, and I'd like them gone."
"On the Old Road. Big as dogs now. Bigger every week. Type 'quests' while you're standing in here and I'll make it official."
"The cellar. Goes down further than the building is tall. Nobody's ever finished counting the stairs. A guild recruiter lives at the bottom. Don't make eye contact."
"Mm," says the barkeep, and goes on polishing.
Brenna sets down seven mugs at once, takes a bow nobody asked for, and fixes you with a look that has ended careers. "Well? I've got forty people to ignore, and you're one of them."

choices.text: Attempt an extremely bad pickup line.

passages.text: "Manners! In a tavern!" She slides a mug in front of you. "On the house. Don't tell the others. They'll expect it."
"Years of practice," she says, "and a lot of resentment." For a moment she almost smiles.
"Is that the best you've got? Last week a man proposed in iambic pentameter. He still got the towel." She demonstrates the towel. Your dignity takes 3 damage.
"Then move," says Brenna. "You're blocking the tips."
"Don't," says Ozzie Plumb, *hic*, "look so happy. In an infinite multiverse there's a tavern where this ale is good. This isn't it." Beside him, his apprentice Timbles offers an apologetic wave.

choices.text: Ask about the beans in his robe.

passages.text: "Regret," says Ozzie, *urp*, "with a hint of regret." Timbles whispers: "It's just ale. He says that every time."

"Every possible tavern. Every possible cellar. Every possible door humming a different tune. I've been to the one where the barrels are in charge. They were fair, honestly." Timbles: "He isn't lying. That's the worst part."

Ozzie accepts the ale with the dignity of a drowning man accepting a rope. "You're the first person in nine dimensions to do that." He presses a dented flask into your hand. "Don't open it near anything you like."
"Magic beans," says Ozzie, patting his robe. "Ten for a gold, normally. For you, free, because I'm tired." Timbles winces. "They're beans."
You take a small bag of suspiciously ordinary beans. "Plant them somewhere with a really tall ceiling," says Ozzie. *hic*
"Go," says Ozzie. "Be somebody else's problem." *hic*
